title: Migrate IT Ticketing from an Employee Portal to Microsoft Teams
summary: Move IT ticketing from an employee portal to Microsoft Teams with practical steps for migration, setup, and smoother support.
body_markdown:
Your employee portal may have looked promising during the demo, but employees still turn to direct messages, random Teams channels, or in-person requests for IT support. As a result, IT teams spend time manually tracking requests, chasing information, and managing conversations across disconnected systems.


Traditional portals require employees to switch platforms to submit and track requests.[Microsoft Teams-native ticketing](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) offers an alternative by bringing support into employees' existing workflows. Unthread converts supported Teams conversations into structured tickets with assignments, SLA tracking, and workflow automation.


Rather than relying on more portal training, organizations can bring IT support directly into Teams. This guide covers the migration process, including implementation steps, automation strategies, and considerations for choosing between portal-based and[Teams-native ticketing](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) .


## **Key Takeaways**


- Traditional employee portals create friction by requiring employees to switch systems, while[Microsoft Teams-native ticketing](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) brings support into employees' existing workflows.
- Unthread's[purpose-built AI agents](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) can resolve routine internal support requests. At Lemonade, its Slack-based implementation achieved[approximately 40% automatic resolution](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) .
- Migrating to Teams-native ticketing involves configuring support channels, connecting existing systems, setting up[automated workflows](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) , and testing integrations. Timelines vary by complexity.
- [AI-powered ticket automation](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) and automated routing reduce repetitive administrative work, with potential savings depending on ticket volume and existing processes.
- Multi-channel support brings requests from Teams, Slack, email, and employee portals into a unified ticketing system.
- [Enterprise security controls](https://unthread.io/security?ref=unthread.io) , including SOC 2 Type II, SSO, SCIM provisioning, and HIPAA availability, help organizations address security and compliance requirements.


## **The Limitations of Traditional Employee Portals for IT Ticketing**


Employee portals promised to centralize internal support requests. In practice, they create more problems than they solve for IT, HR, and operations teams managing day-to-day employee needs.


### **Why Legacy Portals Hinder Productivity**


The fundamental issue with standalone portals is friction. When an employee needs a laptop replacement, password reset, or access request, they face a choice: navigate to a portal they rarely use and fill out a form, or message IT directly in Teams where they already have conversations open. Most choose the path of least resistance.


This creates several downstream problems:


- **Requests fall through cracks** when employees message IT in random channels without formal tracking
- **Context gets lost** as conversations happen in one place while ticket data lives in another
- **Manual triage consumes hours** as IT staff copy information between systems
- **Response times suffer** because there is no automated routing or prioritization
- **Reporting is unreliable** since informal requests never enter the ticketing system


## **Why Microsoft Teams Works for IT Ticketing and Support**


Microsoft Teams has become the operational center for most knowledge workers. Rather than fighting this reality, modern[IT service desk](https://unthread.io/solutions/it-service-desk?ref=unthread.io) approaches work within it.


### **Leveraging Teams for Enhanced IT Service Delivery**


Teams provides the communication infrastructure where employees already spend their workday. Converting this into an IT helpdesk means meeting employees where they are instead of asking them to go somewhere else.


The collaborative advantages compound when IT support happens directly in Teams:


- **Instant messaging eliminates email lag** for time-sensitive requests like account lockouts
- **Thread-based conversations preserve context** that would be lost in separate ticketing systems
- **File sharing and screen sharing** happen naturally within the support conversation
- **Presence indicators** show when IT staff are available for immediate assistance
- **Search functionality** lets employees find answers from previous conversations


### **The Collaborative Advantage of Teams for Support**


When IT support lives in Teams, collaboration happens without friction. An employee reports a laptop issue in the #it-help channel. The IT team can loop in a colleague with specific expertise by simply @mentioning them. If the issue requires procurement approval for a replacement, that conversation happens in the same thread rather than spawning separate email chains.


This native collaboration also supports sensitive requests. The[HR service desk](https://unthread.io/solutions/hr-service-desk?ref=unthread.io) benefits from the same workflow automation while maintaining confidentiality for sensitive employee matters through private ticket routing.


## **How Unthread Supports Microsoft Teams Ticketing**


Unthread transforms Microsoft Teams (and Slack) into a full internal service management platform. Unlike traditional helpdesks that require portal access, Unthread converts conversations directly into structured tickets with routing, SLAs, and automation built in.


### **Seamless IT Support Directly Within Your Teams Workspace**


The core capability is conversational ticketing. When an employee posts a request in a designated support channel, Unthread automatically creates a ticket from that conversation. The employee continues chatting normally while the system tracks everything behind the scenes.


Key features include:


- **Automatic ticket creation** from connected Teams channels
- **AI-powered triage** that routes requests to the appropriate team members based on their content
- **Unified inbox** accessible via Teams showing all open tickets with deep-linking to threads
- **SLA tracking** with automated alerts before breaches occur
- **Private threads** for internal team collaboration on sensitive requests


The system supports multiple intake channels simultaneously. A #it-help channel handles general requests in-channel, while laptop replacement requests might route through a structured workflow for equipment details and shipping address collection. The flexibility means different request types get handled appropriately without forcing everything through the same process.


### **How Unthread Transforms Teams into an AI-Automated Helpdesk**


Beyond ticket tracking, Unthread brings[agentic AI](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai?ref=unthread.io) capabilities that resolve requests automatically. When an employee asks about VPN setup or expense policy, the purpose-built AI agent searches the knowledge base and provides accurate answers without human intervention.


Lemonade deployed Unthread across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams using its Slack-based platform and reports that the platform automatically resolves approximately[40% of incoming tickets](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) . This deflection happens across multiple internal support workflows, not just simple FAQ lookups. Password reset instructions, software request procedures, benefits enrollment guidance, and procurement submission steps all become candidates for AI resolution.


## **Achieving Automated IT Support with Agentic AI in Teams**


Purpose-built AI agents can improve efficiency across modern internal support operations. Rather than simply suggesting articles, agentic AI understands request intent, takes action, and escalates only when necessary.


### **Boosting Efficiency with AI Deflection**


AI deflection means resolving requests without human intervention. AI deflection rates vary based on the types of requests handled, the quality of connected documentation, and the workflows available for automation. Unthread's Lemonade case study reports[approximately 40% automatic resolution](https://unthread.io/blog/case-study-how-lemonade-boosts-efficiency-with-unthread-and-gen-ai/) across multiple internal support teams using its Slack-based platform.


These are not just FAQ lookups. The AI handles multi-step workflows like:


- Explaining the laptop replacement process and triggering the approval workflow
- Walking through access request procedures and creating the provisioning ticket
- Providing expense policy details and linking to the submission form
- Answering benefits questions using HR documentation and escalating only for case-specific issues


The key difference from simple chatbots is that agentic AI takes action. It does not just tell an employee how to request a new company card. It initiates the request, routes it for approval, and updates the employee when appropriate.


### **How AI Reduces Manual IT Work**


Unthread's approach uses a[self-learning knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) that continuously improves. When IT staff resolve tickets manually, the system identifies patterns in frequently asked questions and generates draft documentation for review. This process helps teams turn resolved tickets into documented answers that can support future AI-powered resolutions.


The AI also supports bring-your-own-LLM functionality through MCP integration. Organizations can use internal GPT instances rather than being locked into a single AI provider, addressing data privacy concerns for companies with strict information governance requirements.


## **Streamlining IT Workflows with No-Code Automation in Teams**


Automation transforms IT ticketing from reactive firefighting into proactive service delivery. The goal is eliminating manual steps that add no value while ensuring the right people handle the right requests.


### **Building Custom IT Workflows Without Leaving Teams**


Unthread's[automation builder](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) supports three creation methods:


- **Natural language descriptions** converted directly into working automations
- **Visual drag-and-drop interface** for designing multi-step workflows
- **Custom code and API integrations** for advanced logic when needed


This flexibility matters because internal support workflows vary significantly. Laptop replacement might require manager approval, then procurement review, then finance sign-off. Access requests might need security team validation for certain systems but auto-approve for standard tools. Expense submissions might have different approval chains based on amount thresholds.


### **Automating Routine IT Tasks for Greater Productivity**


Consider common internal support scenarios and their automation potential:


**New Employee Onboarding:**


1. HR creates employee record
2. Automation triggers laptop order based on role
3. IT receives provisioning ticket for accounts
4. Access requests auto-generate for standard tools
5. Training enrollments schedule automatically
6. Week-one check-in creates automatically


**Access Request Processing:**


1. Employee requests access via Teams
2. System identifies required approvers based on application
3. Approval requests route automatically
4. Provisioning workflow initiates upon approval
5. Employee receives confirmation with access instructions


**Equipment Replacement:**


1. Employee reports laptop issue
2. AI provides initial troubleshooting guidance
3. If replacement needed, approval request routes to manager
4. Upon approval, procurement workflow initiates
5. Shipping details collected from employee
6. Status updates provided automatically


[Automated workflows](https://unthread.io/products/automations/?ref=unthread.io) can reduce manual handoffs by routing requests, collecting approvals, and triggering actions in connected systems. Teams can evaluate their effectiveness by comparing resolution times, manual intervention rates, and SLA performance before and after implementation.


## **Unifying Multi-Channel IT Support Beyond Just Teams and Portals**


Employees do not always use the same channel for every request. Some prefer Teams, others use Slack, and many still send emails. A modern internal support platform needs to handle all intake channels while maintaining unified visibility.


### **Consolidating All Support Channels for IT Teams**


Unthread provides omni-channel intake that brings requests together regardless of source:


- **Teams channels** for employees who live in Microsoft environments
- **Slack messages** for companies using both platforms
- **Email forwarding** that creates tickets from support inbox messages
- **Employee portal** for self-service submissions when appropriate
- **Live chat widgets** for internal portals or intranet sites


The unified inbox shows all open requests in one view with deep-linking to original conversations. IT staff do not need to monitor multiple platforms or manually consolidate information.


### **Bridging Gaps Between Email, Chat, and Teams for Unified Support**


The[shared email inbox](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox?ref=unthread.io) capability addresses the email challenge specifically. Many internal support requests still arrive via email, especially from employees accustomed to that workflow. Rather than asking everyone to change behavior immediately, Unthread forwards support emails into designated channels.


Each email creates a private discussion thread where IT staff can collaborate internally, add tags and priorities, and link related tasks. Responses sent from the Teams thread appear as email replies to the employee. This bridges the gap during migration while gradually shifting employees toward Teams-native interaction.


## **Real-Time IT Performance Monitoring with AI Analytics in Teams**


Visibility into internal support performance enables continuous improvement. Without metrics, IT leaders cannot identify bottlenecks, justify staffing decisions, or demonstrate value to the organization.


### **Gaining Insights into IT Service Performance with AI**


Unthread's[analytics platform](https://unthread.io/products/analytics?ref=unthread.io) provides real-time tracking of key metrics:


- **Support volume** broken down by request type, team, and time period
- **SLA breach tracking** with alerts before deadlines are missed
- **AI deflection rate** showing percentage of requests resolved without human intervention
- **Response time and resolution time** by category and assignee
- **CSAT and NPS scores** collected automatically after ticket resolution
- **Recurring issue patterns** identified automatically through AI analysis


Unthread's analytics platform helps internal support teams track request volume, SLA performance, AI deflection, and recurring issues across connected support channels. Teams can use these insights to identify bottlenecks, evaluate automation effectiveness, and improve knowledge base coverage. Support data can also be integrated with business intelligence tools such as Looker, Tableau, and Hex.


### **Measuring and Optimizing IT Support in Your Teams Workspace**


Practical use of analytics drives meaningful improvement. For example, if analytics reveal that password reset requests account for a large share of ticket volume despite existing self-service documentation, IT teams can investigate whether the instructions are difficult to find or insufficiently clear.


Export capabilities support integration with business intelligence tools like Looker, Tableau, and Hex via API. For organizations with established BI infrastructure, raw ticket data flows into existing dashboards alongside other operational metrics.


## **Security and Compliance for Enterprise IT Teams in Microsoft Teams**


Migrating IT ticketing to Teams raises legitimate security questions. Internal support conversations often contain sensitive information: employee data, system credentials, procurement details, and more.


### **Ensuring Data Security in Your Teams-Based IT Helpdesk**


Unthread maintains enterprise security standards that meet requirements for regulated industries. Unthread provides[enterprise security](https://unthread.io/security?ref=unthread.io) capabilities that include:


- **SOC 2 Type II independent auditing** with regular independent security audits
- **TLS 1.3 encryption in transit** and AES-256 encryption at rest
- **SAML 2.0 single sign-on** and SCIM user provisioning
- **Role-based access controls** with granular permissions per team
- **Regular third-party penetration testing** for vulnerability assessment
- **HIPAA Business Associate Agreements** for eligible healthcare organizations


The privacy-first AI approach means Unthread does not train models on customer data. Organizations concerned about data handling can use their own LLM through MCP integration rather than sending information to external AI services.


## **Migrating Your IT Ticketing: A Step-by-Step Approach with Unthread**


The migration from employee portal to Teams-native ticketing follows a predictable pattern. Understanding the phases helps set realistic expectations and ensures nothing falls through cracks during transition.


### **Seamless Transition to Teams-Native IT Support**


**Phase 1: Preparation (Week 1-2)**


Audit the existing portal to understand ticket volume, request categories, and current SLAs. Export knowledge base content and document existing integrations. Select a pilot team (usually IT power users) for initial rollout.


Key deliverables:


- Migration plan with timeline and milestones
- Stakeholder communication plan
- Pilot team selection and training schedule


**Phase 2: Configuration (Week 2-3)**


Deploy Unthread in the Teams environment and configure support channels. Connect integrations with identity providers (Azure AD, Okta), HRIS systems, and existing tools. Import knowledge base content and configure AI training data.


Migrating from an employee portal to[Microsoft Teams-native ticketing](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support?ref=unthread.io) involves configuring support channels, connecting existing systems, setting up automation rules, and testing workflows. Implementation timelines depend on the complexity of the organization's existing ticketing environment, integrations, and approval processes.


**Phase 3: Testing (Week 3-4)**


Validate AI response accuracy with the pilot team. Test integration workflows end-to-end (create ticket in Teams, verify sync to external systems). Configure SLA alerting and verify escalation paths.


Target benchmarks:


- AI accuracy validation on FAQ-type requests
- All integrations functioning correctly
- SLA alerts triggering before breaches


**Phase 4: Parallel Run (Week 5-6)**


Run Teams ticketing alongside the existing portal. Direct new requests to Teams while continuing to service existing portal tickets. Monitor adoption rates and address friction points.


**Phase 5: Cutover (Week 7+)**


Decommission the legacy portal once Teams adoption stabilizes. Archive historical tickets for reference. Communicate the change organization-wide with clear instructions for submitting requests.
